record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Find a nonsupersolvable central hyperplane arrangement for which the lower central series formula product_{j>=1}(1 - t^j)^{phi_j} = Hilb_A(-t) holds; equivalently, find a Koszul Orlik-Solomon algebra without a quadratic Groebner basis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a central hyperplane arrangement in a complex vector space, and let $A = \mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{A})$ denote its Orlik–Solomon algebra (the quotient of the exterior algebra on generators $e_H$, one per hyperplane $H \in \mathcal{A}$, by the ideal generated by $\partial(e_{H_1}\cdots e_{H_k})$ for every dependent subarrangement $\{H_1,\dots,H_k\}$). Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_A(t) = \sum_i \dim(A_i) t^i$ be its Hilbert series. The complement $M(\mathcal{A})$ has fundamental group whose lower central series quotients have ranks $\phi_j$. The arrangement is said to satisfy the lower central series (LCS) formula if
$$\prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - t^j)^{\phi_j} \;=\; \mathrm{Hilb}_A(-t).$$
An arrangement is supersolvable if its intersection lattice admits a maximal chain of modular elements.

Exhibit a central hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ that is not supersolvable but for which the LCS formula above holds; equivalently, exhibit a central arrangement whose Orlik–Solomon algebra is Koszul yet admits no presentation with a quadratic Gröbner basis (or prove that no such arrangement exists, thereby establishing that Koszulness of $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{A})$ implies supersolvability of $\mathcal{A}$).
artifact.status_search_result: The converse direction—whether Koszulness of the Orlik–Solomon algebra of a central arrangement forces supersolvability—is widely cited as an open problem. It has been verified for several special classes (root ideal arrangements, Dirichlet arrangements, matroids with disjoint minimal broken circuits, and others), but no example is known of a nonsupersolvable arrangement with Koszul Orlik–Solomon algebra, nor is there a general proof of the implication.

status_evidence.title: Supersolvability and the Koszul property of root ideal arrangements
status_evidence.snippet: OS(A_I) has the Koszul property if and only if A_I is supersolvable.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalence is established only for root ideal arrangements, not in general.

status_evidence.title: Koszulness and supersolvability for Dirichlet arrangements
status_evidence.snippet: The cone over a Dirichlet arrangement is supersolvable if and only if its Orlik-Solomon algebra is Koszul, previously shown for four other classes.
status_evidence.claim: The converse is verified for several special classes but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Koszulity, supersolvability, and Stirling representations
status_evidence.snippet: Whether the converse is true is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explicitly refers to the converse as an open problem.
